children: According to CNBC, the average rate on the 30-year fixed mortgage rose to 7.45% on Thursday, according to Mortgage News Daily, after bond yields surged. The rate was up 19 basis points from 7.26% the day before, and Mortgage News Daily said it re-ran its survey in the afternoon as the 10-year Treasury yield moved higher. Matthew Graham, chief operating officer at Mortgage News Daily, said 7% was first broken on September 10 after inflation reports increased the risk of the Fed rate hike seen last week, and he said Fed comments, higher oil prices and stronger economic data have added to the pressure since then. He also said there was no obvious catalyst for the afternoon bond selloff. Freddie Mac reported Thursday morning that the rate had just crossed 7%, but that figure was an average of the last week. The 30-year fixed fell as low as 5.99% at the end of February and began rising at the start of the war with Iran.

title: 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate Jumps To 7.45%
